text: Verify screening history; confirm last mammogram and next due date; if overdue, explain the importance of screening and offer help with booking. If data is missing, confirm history before sending reminders.

45–49: Explain screening and booking. 50–54: Check last screening date. 55–59: Check referral and appointment after changing doctor. 60–64: Encourage continued screening. 65–69: Identify barriers. 70–74: Help arrange screening; do not exclude by age. 75+: Support an individual decision with a doctor.
≥1 examination in 24 months: Check referral and appointment; offer gynaecologist support. 0 examinations: Check for a current gynaecologist; otherwise offer GP or coordinator support.
First invitation: Explain screening purpose and booking. Repeat invitation: Check whether screening is completed or booked; identify barriers and offer assistance.

Less than 12 months: Check for duplicate invitations or existing/completed screening. 12–23 months: Offer alternative support if needed. 24 months or more: Update contact details, verify screening history, and help choose a centre and book.

At least one recorded participation: Build on existing preventive care experience; offer a shared prevention calendar, reminders, and booking assistance. | No recorded participation: Explain the value of preventive screening in the absence of symptoms and offer practical assistance.

A: Verify whether screening occurred elsewhere or before the available observation period; if screening is needed, explain the process, answer questions, and help with booking. | N: Establish the date of the previous mammogram and verify when the next examination is due.

Zero recorded contacts in 12 months: Offer direct outreach and coordinator assistance rather than relying on an upcoming medical visit. | Healthcare contacts but no preventive care: Offer support through the current healthcare team. | High number of contacts: Check for healthcare-related burden and offer an approach that minimizes additional visits.

At least one preventive examination: Test whether a shared prevention calendar and simple reminders are useful. | No recorded examination: Offer explanations and practical assistance without assumptions about motivation, responsibility, or finances.

2–5 years or more than 5 years: Verify the current relationship with the practice and offer support through that practice. | Less than 2 years: Check transfer of previous screening information and clarify responsibility for follow-up.

All territorial areas: Identify potentially suitable, verified screening centers; confirm the current address, booking options, available appointments, and preferences regarding distance, timing, and earliest availability.

Shorter insurance duration: Check whether screening occurred under a previous health insurance provider. | Longer insurance duration: Use the variable to assess the completeness of screening history, not to justify more intensive persuasion.

A: Verify the current gynecologist and offer involvement of the practice, particularly if a preventive examination is also recorded. | N: Offer support through a GP or care coordinator; do not discontinue support because the client has no registered gynecologist.

Longer registration: Offer involvement of the current GP, especially if preferred by the client or if no gynecologist is available. | Shorter registration: Verify transfer of information about the last mammogram and continuity of follow-up care.

At least one preventive examination: Verify the current GP and offer referral checks and booking assistance. | No preventive examinations but other healthcare contacts: Offer support through the current healthcare team or a coordinator instead of automatically waiting for another preventive visit.

A: Verify the current GP and whether their practice can assist with screening. | N: Offer support through the current gynecologist or a coordinator who can verify the booking procedure and the screening center's referral requirements.

Zero previous invitations: Explain the purpose of screening, outline the examination and booking process, and offer one clear next step. | One previous invitation: Verify whether screening has already been completed or booked; if not, identify barriers and offer practical assistance. | Multiple previous invitations: Check screening history and current appointment status, then identify unresolved barriers and offer a more suitable support channel, such as coordinator assistance or help through the client's current healthcare provider. | General rule: The number of previous invitations does not prove screening refusal or lack of motivation. Avoid duplicate outreach and coordinate all interventions into one support plan.
